description: Sourced default assumptions for the HeatHunter public diagnostic model and screening money estimates. Every entry is an ASSUMPTION, never a measurement of a simulated fault. Entries with verified=false are illustrative, user-adjustable defaults that could not be tied to an authoritative source.

source.dataset: SAP 2012 v9.92 (Oct 2013, with RdSAP Dec 2014), Table 1f
source.citation: BRE (2014). The Government's Standard Assessment Procedure for Energy Rating of Dwellings, 2012 edition, Table 1f.
source.notes: Indicative TMP values: low 100, medium 250, high 450 kJ/m2K. 'Medium' is used for HH09 (masonry cavity walls, suspended timber floor). Room capacitance = TMP x documented floor area + air capacity. This is the engine's absolute-scale anchor.

source.dataset: Air density about 1.2 kg/m3 x specific heat about 1005 J/(kg.K)
source.notes: Added to each room's fabric capacitance; it is small relative to the fabric term.

source.provider: ASHRAE via U.S. DOE EnergyPlus documentation
source.citation: ASHRAE Handbook of Fundamentals (2001 ch.26; 2005 ch.27), as tabulated in EnergyPlus ZoneInfiltration:EffectiveLeakageArea.
source.notes: One-storey house (HH09 is a bungalow), shelter class 3 ('other buildings across the street'). The public model's linear wind sensitivity beta is the least-squares slope/intercept of sqrt(1 + (Cw/Cs) w^2 / dT_ref) over the wind range. dT_ref = 12 K is a HeatHunter assumption for heating-off night tests. Beta converts the measured windy-night increase in heat loss into calm-night infiltration conductance.

source.citation: ISO 6946 internal surface resistances (2 x 0.13 m2K/W, horizontal heat flow); ISO 10456/CIBSE Guide A conductivities: dense block 1.13 W/mK, gypsum plaster 0.57 W/mK.
source.notes: R = 0.26 + 0.100/1.13 + 2 x 0.013/0.57 = 0.394 m2K/W, so U is about 2.5 W/m2K. HH09's partition construction is unpublished. Coupling = U x plan-derived shared-boundary length x 2.4 m. Passive cooling data cannot identify coupling, so it is fixed, not fitted. It is deliberately a different plausible construction from the simulator's assumption, so the benchmark tests model mismatch honestly.

source.dataset: SAP 2012 v9.92 (Oct 2013, with RdSAP Dec 2014), Table 6e
source.citation: BRE (2014). The Government's Standard Assessment Procedure for Energy Rating of Dwellings, 2012 edition, Table 6e (p. 217): double-glazed, air filled, wood or PVC-U frame, 12 mm gap.
source.notes: HH09 is documented only as 'Double glazing'. SAP says to take double glazing as air-filled without low-E unless known otherwise; the gap is unpublished, so the 12 mm column is used (6 mm: 3.1, 16 mm+: 2.7). Applies to the whole window opening including frame. Glass has negligible thermal mass, so this path cools the room AIR directly (in parallel with infiltration), not the fabric. Window conductance = U x documented window area. No curtain adjustment is applied. Deliberately the published default, not the simulator's own window coefficient.

source.dataset: Bathroom exhaust fans resource guide (50 cfm intermittent example)
source.notes: 50 cfm x 1.699 = 84.95 m3/h of delivered airflow, the same public value the simulator uses. It is a hypothetical fan, not an HH09 measurement.

source.provider: UK Data Service (SMETER Phase 2), derived by HeatHunter
source.dataset: SMETER Phase 2 central weather station air temperature, calendar year 2020
source.citation: Allinson, D. et al. (2024). Technical Evaluation of SMETER Technologies Project Phase 2 Data. UK Data Service. SN 856978.
source.notes: Sum over 2020 of max(0, 15.5 - daily mean air temperature). All 366 days are complete; base 15.5 degC is the UK convention. The station is 5.2 km from HH09. Cross-check: AHDB reports North West England 1761 (May 2019-Apr 2020) and 1825 (May 2020-Apr 2021). Reproduce with scripts/derive_hh09_money_inputs.py. It is one year only and not a long-term mean.

source.provider: UK Data Service (SMETER Phase 2), derived by HeatHunter
source.dataset: SMETER Phase 2 central weather station wind speed, October-April 2019-2021
source.notes: Mean of all half-hourly October-April readings. It converts a draft's calm-air excess into a seasonal average excess (the public infiltration model is linear in wind).

HH09's documented Intergas Combi Compact ECO RF 30 gas boiler: winter seasonal efficiency 86.7% (SAP annual 88.8%). This is a product rating, not an in-situ measurement. Heat loss is divided by this to give gas energy.

source.dataset: Energy price cap, 1 October - 31 December 2026, Direct Debit average (England, Scotland and Wales)
source.notes: Marginal unit rate only. The standing charge (29.68 p/day) is excluded because it does not change with heat loss. Regional rates differ slightly.

source.provider: Bank of England (spot rate, republished by Pound Sterling Live)
source.dataset: GBP/USD daily spot reference rate, 22 October 2026
source.notes: Converts UK costs to the API's USD convention. Exchange rates move daily.

source.dataset: Whole-house professional draught-proofing, typically quoted at GBP 150-300
source.notes: UNVERIFIED illustrative default; it should be adjustable by the user. It is a whole-house figure, so draught-proofing a single room may cost less. The Energy Saving Trust pages could not be retrieved.

add_insulation.unit: GBP per m2 of exterior wall

source.dataset: Installed internal wall insulation, about GBP 60-100 per m2 (2026)
source.notes: UNVERIFIED illustrative default; it should be adjustable by the user. It excludes making good, moving radiators and decoration. Multiplied by the room's assumed exterior wall area.

source.dataset: Exterior wall lengths derived from printed room dimensions
source.notes: ASSUMPTION used only to size the illustrative insulation cost. Living = 4.36 + 3.15, Kitchen = 3.14 + 1.83, Bedroom = 3.80 + 3.11, Hall = 1.14 (entrance side). Area = length x 2.4 m minus documented window area.
